items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4067

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the civil service law, in relation
to compensation, benefits and other terms and conditions of employment
of certain state officers and employees; to implement agreements
between the state and an employee organization; making an
appropriation for the purpose of effectuating certain provisions
thereof; and to repeal certain provisions of the civil service law
relating thereto (Part A); and to amend the civil service law and the
correction law, in relation to salaries; to implement agreements
between the state and an employee organization; to repeal certain
provisions of such laws relating thereto; and making an appropriation
for the purpose of effectuating certain provisions hereof (Part B)

 PURPOSE :

Part A of this bill would implement the terms of a collective
bargaining agreement ("the Agreement"), entered into pursuant to
Article 14 of the Civil Service Law ("CSL"), between the Executive
Branch of the State of New York and the employee organization
representing members of the collective negotiating unit designated as
the Professional, Scientific and Technical Services Unit ("PS&T
Unit").

Part B of this bill would provide the State's approximately 11,000
annual-salaried unrepresented Executive Branch employees who are
prohibited from collective negotiations by Article 14 of the CSL,
including managerial or confidential ("M/C") employees, with the same
increases in compensation received by employees represented by
employee organizations.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Part A of the Bill:

Section 1 of Part A of this bill would repeal subparagraph 1 of CSL §
130(1)(c) and replace it with new subparagraphs 1, 2, and 3 to provide
new salary schedules for officers and employees in the PS&T Unit for
the period April 2, 2016 to April 1, 2019.

Section 2 of Part A of this bill would provide for increases in
compensation for covered members of the PS&T Unit, including: (i) a
two percent basic annual salary increase effective April 7, 2016 for
officers and employees on the administrative payroll, and effective
March 31, 2016 for officers and employees on the institutional
payroll; (ii) a two percent basic annual salary increase effective
April 6, 2017 for officers and employees on the administrative
payroll, and effective March 30, 2017 for officers and employees on
the institutional payroll; (iii) a two percent basic annual salary
increase effective April 5, 2018 for officers and employees on the
administrative payroll, and effective March 29, 2018 for officers and
employees on the institutional payroll; and (iv) performance
advancement payments to covered members of the PS&T Unit pursuant to
CSL § 131(6).

This section also would give the Director of the Budget and the
Director of Employee Relations discretion to withhold all or a portion
of a unit members' salary increase, where appropriate or warranted.

Section 3 of Part A of this bill would continue existing location
compensation for employees whose principal place of employment is
located in the counties of Monroe, Rockland, Westchester, Nassau,
Suffolk, Dutchess, Putnam, and Orange, or the city of New York. For
the county of Monroe, only employees who were eligible on March 31,
1985 to receive location compensation shall be eligible for continued
location compensation of $200 per year. Employees in New York City or
in the counties of Rockland, Westchester, Nassau or Suffolk continue
to receive location compensation at the annual rate of $3,026.
Employees in the counties of Dutchess, Putnam or Orange continue to
receive location compensation at the annual rate of $1,513. If an
employee is on an approved leave of absence for less than one year or
participates in an employer program to work part-time during the
summer months, prior eligibility for location pay would continue upon
return to full-time State service in Monroe County.

Section 4 of Part A of this bill would continue location compensation
for certain officers and employees of the Hudson Valley Developmental
Disabilities Services Office.

Section 5 of Part A of this bill would continue special assignment to
duty pay in the form of an annual lump sum payment to certain
employees in a particular assignment deemed qualified under the terms
of the Agreement. This payment will expire on April 1, 2019, unless an
extension is negotiated by the parties.

Section 6 of Part A of this bill would provide for an annual lump sum
payment to longterm seasonal employees in an amount specified by, and
subject to, the qualifying criteria established by the Agreement.
This payment will expire on March 31, 2019.

Section 7 of Part A of this bill would authorize contributions to
employee dependent care accounts in amounts and for the time period
designated in the Agreement.

Section 8 of Part A of this bill would provide for the payment and
publication of grievance and arbitration settlements and awards
between the State and the employee organization representing employees
who are members of the PS&T Unit.

Section 9 of Part A of this bill would provide that statewide
labor-management committees, administered pursuant to the terms of the
Agreement, shall be responsible for studying and making
recommendations concerning major issues of productivity, the quality
of work life and health benefits, and implementing the agreements
reached.

Section 10 of Part A of this bill would provide for inconvenience pay
to continue at a rate of $575 per year for eligible employees who work
four or more hours between the hours of 6:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m.

Section 11 of Part A of this bill would provide for the payment of a
lump sum Firearms Training and Safety Incentive to qualified peace
officers who are members of the PS&T Unit pursuant to the terms of a
program collectively negotiated between the State and the employee
organization representing such members. This program will expire on
April 1, 2019, unless an extension is negotiated by the parties.

Section 12 of Part A of this bill would provide for the payment of a
lump sum uniform allowance to certain employees of the Office of Fire
Prevention and Control in the Fire Protection Specialist title series
if there is a policy in place that requires employees to wear
uniforms, in accordance with the terms of a negotiated side letter to
the Agreement. This allowance will expire on April 1, 2019, unless an
extension is negotiated by the parties.

Section 13 of Part A of this bill would require that, prior to any
salary increases and benefit modifications provided by this bill, the
Director of the Budget and the State Comptroller must receive a letter
from the Director of the Governor's Office of-Employee Relations
certifying that the Agreement has been ratified by the membership.


Section 14 of Part A of this bill would set the date upon which
incumbent members of the PS&T Unit would receive the salary increases
provided by the Agreement.

Section 15 of Part A of this bill would authorize a lump sum payment
for retroactive salary increases and compensation modifications deemed
in effect on April 1, 2016, as provided for by Part A of this bill.

Section 16 of Part A of this bill would authorize the State
Comptroller to pay any amounts required by this bill during the fiscal
year commencing April 1, 2016 through March 31, 2018 for any state
department or agency from any appropriation or other funds available
to such state department or agency for personal service or for any
other related employee benefits during such fiscal year. To the extent
that such appropriations in any fund are insufficient, the Director of
the Budget is authorized to allocate to the various departments and
agencies, from any appropriations available in any fund, the amounts
necessary to pay such amounts.

Section 17 of Part A of this bill would provide that employees who
participate in a special annuity program under Article 8-C of the
Education Law shall not suffer any reduction of the salary adjustment
to which they are otherwise entitled under the program, as a result of
an increase in compensation provided for in Part A of this bill.

Section 18 of Part A of this bill would provide for a lump sum
appropriation for personal and non-personal services, and for salary
adjustments for use by state departments or agencies, to carry out the
provisions of Part A of this bill.

Section 19 of Part A of this bill would provide that certain funds for
statewide labor management committees are appropriated for use by the
state departments' or agencies' Labor Management Committees to carry
out the provisions of Part A of this bill.

Section 20 of Part A of this bill would require it to become effective
immediately, and deem it to have been in full force and effect on and
after April 2, 2016. Appropriations made by Part A of this bill would
remain in full force and effect for liabilities incurred through March
31, 2018.

Part B of the Bill:

Section 1 of Part B of this bill would repeal CSL § 130(1)(d) and
replace it with .a new paragraph (d), establishing new salary
schedules for competitive, noncompetitive, and labor class employees
designated M/C, or who are otherwise not in, or excluded from
representation rights in, any recognized or certified negotiating
unit.

Section 2 of Part B of this bill would repeal Correction Law § 19(1)
and replace it with a new subdivision 1 providing new salary schedules
for superintendents of correctional facilities.

Section 3 of Part B of this bill would authorize an increase in basic
annual salary of: (i) two percent effective April 1, 2016; (ii) four
percent effective April 1, 2017, consisting of two percent pursuant to
the parity pay increase provided by Part H of Chapter 55 of the Laws
of 2015 and two percent pursuant to a general salary increase for 2017
in accordance with this bill; and (iii) three percent effective April
1, 2018, consisting of one percent pursuant to the parity pay increase
provided by Part H of Chapter 55 of the Laws of 2015 and two percent
pursuant to a general salary increase for 2018 in accordance with this
bill. Additionally, this section would provide for performance
advances, merit awards and longevity payments for non-statutorily paid
employees.
Sections 4 and 5 of Part B of this bill would provide salary increases
and lump sum payments consistent with the salary increases provided in
Section 3 of Part B of this bill for certain State officers and
employees in the Division of State Police, certain State employees in
the State University of New York, and certain employees of the
contract colleges at Cornell and Alfred Universities.

Section 6 of Part B of this bill would continue existing location
compensation for certain employees whose principal place of employment
is located the counties of Monroe, Rockland, Westchester, Nassau,
Suffolk, Dutchess, Orange and, Putnam, or the city of New York. For
the county of Monroe, only employees hired before March 31, 1985 shall
be eligible for continued location compensation of $200 per year.
Employees in New York City, or in the counties of Rockland,
Westchester, Nassau or Suffolk shall receive location compensation at
the annual rate of $3,026. Employees in the counties of Dutchess,
Putnam or Orange continue to receive location compensation at the
annual rate of $1,513.

Section 7 of Part B of this bill would continue location compensation
for certain officers and employees of the Hudson Valley Developmental
Disabilities Services Office.

Section 8 of Part B of this bill would provide for the continuation of
an overtime meal allowance for employees covered by this part.

Section 9 of Part B of this bill would continue authorization for
payment of grievance settlements and awards pursuant to Executive
Order No. 42, and title 9, part 560 of the official compilation of
codes, rules and regulations of the state of New York, which applies
to M/C employees.

Section 10 of Part B of this bill would authorize the State
Comptroller to make payments required during the fiscal years
commencing April 1, 2016 through March 31, 2018 for any state
department or agency from any appropriation or other funds available
to such state department or agency for personal service or for any
other related employee benefits during such fiscal year. To the extent
that such appropriations in any fund are insufficient, the Director of
the Budget is authorized to allocate to the various departments and
agencies, from any appropriations available in any fund, the amounts
necessary to pay such amounts.

Section 11 of Part B of this bill would provide that employees who
participate in a special annuity program under Article 8-C of the
Education Law shall not suffer any reduction of the salary adjustment
to which they are otherwise entitled under the program, as a result of
an increase in compensation provided for in this bill.

Section 12 of Part B of this bill would provide that salary increases,
pursuant to this bill, shall be effective on the first day of the
first pay period nearest to the effective date of any such salary
increase.

Section 13 of Part B of this bill would authorize a lump sum payment
for retroactive salary increases and compensation modifications deemed
in effect on April 1, 2016, as provided for by this bill.

Section 14 of Part B of this bill would provide that the Director of
the Budget may withhold any salary increase in order to: (i) reflect
the job performance of an officer or of an employee; (ii) maintain
appropriate salary relationships among employees; (iii) reduce state
expenditures to acceptable levels; or (iv) determine whether such
increase is not warranted or appropriate. Additionally, this section
would provide that nothing in this bill shall alter the authority of
the Director of the Budget to withhold a parity pay increase in
accordance with the authority granted to the Director of the Budget by
Part H of Chapter 55 of the Laws of 2015. Further, as a result of an
exercise of the Director of the Budget's authority under Part B of
this bill, or Part H of Chapter 55 of the Laws of 2015, to withhold
any increase, the salary schedules in section one may be implemented
and/or modified by the Director of the Budget, consistent with the
provision or withholding of salary increases.

Section 15 of Part B of this bill would provide for a lump sum
appropriation for personal and non-personal services, and for salary
adjustments for use by State departments or agencies, to carry out the
provisions of this part.

Section 16 of Part B of this bill would appropriate additional funding
to supplement currently available appropriations to carry out the
benefits and training and development programs. In addition, funding
is included to cover the pro rata M/C share of negotiated programs.

Section 17 of Part B of this bill would require it take effect
immediately, and deem it to have been in full force and effect on and
after April 1, 2016. Appropriations made by Part B of this bill would
remain in full force and effect for liabilities incurred through March
31, 2018.

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT :

Part A of the Bill:

Enactment of Part A of this bill is necessary to implement the
provisions of the collective bargaining agreement, negotiated by the
Executive Branch of the State of New York with the Public Employees
Federation, AFL-CIO, on behalf of members of the PS&T Unit.
Approximately 47,000 annual salaried Executive Branch employees are
covered by the Agreement, which includes a variety of professional,
scientific and technical titles including information technology
professionals, nurses, accountants, lawyers, engineers, and
physicians.

The prior agreement governing these employees expired on April 1,
2016. This new Agreement covers the time period April 2, 2016, to
April 1, 2019. Under Article 14 of the CSL, the Agreement is binding
on all parties to it. Part A of this bill incorporates the terms of
that Agreement related to salary increases and benefit modifications
and appropriates funds necessary to pay for it in accordance with the
State's obligations.

Part B of this Bill:

Enactment of Part B of this bill is necessary to establish terms and
conditions of employment for approximately 11,000 annual-salaried
Executive Branch M/C and other unrepresented employees.

Part B of this bill would provide M/C and other unrepresented
employees with compensation increases and payments that are comparable
to recently negotiated increases and payments for certain represented
employees. Such parity is essential to maintain proper salary
relationships and mitigate salary compression, assure productivity,
maintain good morale, and to allow for the recruitment and retention
of competent staff.

 BUDGET IMPLICATIONS :

Part A of this bill would provide appropriations totaling
approximately $343 million to pay for the cost of the Agreement during
the period April 2, 2016 to March 31, 2018.

Part B of this bill would provide appropriations totaling
approximately $112 million to pay for its cost during the period April
1, 2016 to March 31, 2018.

summary: Relates to the compensation, benefits and others terms and conditions of employment of certain state officers and employees; implements agreements between the state and an employee organization; relates to salaries of certain employees; and appropriates $109,000,000 therefor.
